content.title: About
content.content: Pasta with vegetables, no sauce is a dish made from cooked durum wheat pasta and fresh vegetables that are steamed or lightly sautéed without any sauces, dressings, or added oils. The vegetables retain most of their nutrients, while the pasta provides energy through complex carbohydrates.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish is popular in low‑calorie diets because it contains no fatty sauces.
Vegetables such as broccoli, carrots, zucchini, and bell pepper are rich in vitamins A, C, and K.
Durum wheat pasta (semolina) has a lower glycemic index than regular white pasta.
In traditional Mediterranean cuisine the dish is often finished with a drizzle of olive oil, but the no‑sauce version highlights the pure flavors of the ingredients.
It can be easily adapted for vegan and gluten‑free diets by using gluten‑free or legume‑based pasta.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Pasta provides a steady release of energy, helping to maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Rich in vitamins and minerals
items.content: The vegetables supply vitamins A, C, K, as well as potassium, magnesium, and folate.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber from the vegetables and whole‑grain pasta promotes healthy bowel function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Absence of sauce and oil makes the dish suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Phytonutrients in the vegetables (e.g., lutein, beta‑carotene) help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Wheat allergy or gluten intolerance
items.content: Durum wheat pasta can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Excess sodium from added salt
items.content: If the dish is seasoned with salt, monitor the amount to avoid high sodium intake.

items.title: Digestive discomfort from high fiber
items.content: Large portions of vegetables may cause gas or bloating in individuals with sensitive gastrointestinal tracts.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pasta with vegetables hot or warm. Cut the vegetables into bite‑size pieces, steam or lightly sauté them in a dry pan, then toss with cooked pasta. Optionally garnish with fresh herbs (basil, parsley) or a splash of lemon juice for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared pasta with vegetables in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Pasta and vegetables can be stored separately: dry pasta in a cool, dry place; vegetables in the fridge in a vented bag with a small amount of moisture.
